newsitem.title: USA: St. Joseph adopts rights plan, creates unit.
newsitem.headline: St. Joseph adopts rights plan, creates unit.

text.p: St. Joseph Light & Power Co said it established an investment subsidiary and adopted a new shareholder rights plan.
The subsidiary, called SJLP Inc, "will seek both active and non-active investments in non-utility areas as a means of increasing shareholder returns," the utility said.

The new rights plan declares a dividend of one common share purchase right for each outstanding share of common stock. The rights, to be distributed December 4, will entitle the holders to purchase for each right one-half of one share of common stock at a purchase price of $35, it said.

The rights are exercisable only if a person or group acquires 15 percent or more of the common stock, or announces a tender offer which would result in ownership by a person or group of 15 percent or more of the common stock.

The company would be entitled to redeem the rights at a cost of $0.01 each at any time before the 10th business day, subject to an extension, after a public announcement that a 15 percent position had been acquired, it said.
The rights will expire December 4, 2006, unless redeemed earlier.
